SUMMARY
This summary aims to give you an overview of the information contained in this
Prospectus. As this is a summary, it does not contain all the information that may be
important to you. You should read the entire Prospectus before you decide to invest in our
H Shares. There are risks associated with any investment. Some of the particular risks in
investing in our Shares are set out in the section headed “Risk Factors” in this
Prospectus. You should read that section carefully before you decide to invest in our
H Shares. Various expressions used in this section are defined in the sections headed
“Definitions” and “Glossary” in this Prospectus.
OVERVIEW
We are a leading global fabless IC design company focused on offering innovative,
reliable and power-efficient interconnect solutions for cloud computing and AI infrastructure.
We provide interconnect chips including memory interconnect chips and PCIe (peripheral
component interconnect express)/CXL (compute express link) interconnect chips to industry
leading customers for a wide range of end applications in data centers, servers and computers.
Intermsofrevenuein2024,wehaveemergedasthelargestmemoryinterconnectchipsupplier
in the world, with 36.8% market share, according to Frost & Sullivan.
We provide a full range of DDR2 to DDR5 (the second to the fifths generations of double
data rate technologies) memory interface chips together with DDR5 supporting chips including
SPD (Serial Presence Detect), TS (Temperature Sensor), and PMIC (Power Management

Interconnectivityplaysanincreasinglyvitalroleindatatransmissionwiththeevolvement
of modern data infrastructure.As processing power accelerated at a remarkable rate, it created
a fundamental imbalance across computer systems. Processors began to operate so quickly that
they were often held back by the slower pace of improvement in memory bandwidth, creating
a critical performance bottleneck. Memory interface chips emerged as critical interconnect
solutions to overcome this bottleneck, enabling memory to keep pace with computing and
unlocking maximum system performance.
The need for a data-centric infrastructure is driven by the demands of managing
unprecedented volumes of data with high quality and overcoming the discrepancy between
processor speed and memory bandwidth, while at increasingly faster transfer rates and across
anew,heterogeneoussystemarchitecture.Thisarchitectureisnolongercenteredsolelyaround
CPUs but now includes GPUs and a range of interconnected devices in increasingly complex
configurations. In addition, it has reshaped system design around three pillars: computing,
memory and interconnectivity.The importance of interconnect is expected to continue to grow,
as it underpins the efficiency, reliability, low-latency and scalability of data-centric systems.

OUR TECHNOLOGIES
Memory Interface Technologies
Through rigorous R&D, we have established ourselves as one of the few global suppliers
capableofdeliveringacomprehensivesetofmemoryinterfacechipsspanningDDR2toDDR5.
In the DDR4 generation, our invention of the “1+9” (one RCD chip and nine DB chips)
distributed buffer memory subsystem architecture was adopted by JEDEC as the international
standard for LRDIMM, which significantly reduces the load effect between the CPU and
DRAM, lowers signal transmission loss and addresses the trade-off between large memory
capacity and high speed. In the DDR5 generation, it evolved into the “1+10” (one RCD chip
and ten DB chips), continuing to serve as the international standard for LRDIMM and has
further developed into the international standard for a new type of high bandwidth memory
module MRDIMM equipped with one MRCD chip and ten MDB chips.
At the industry forefront, our latest DDR5 Gen 5 RCD supports data rates of up to 8,000
MT/s, while our high-bandwidth memory interface chips DDR5 Gen 2 MRCD/MDB launched
in early 2025 achieve data rate of 12,800 MT/s, the highest data rates in the industry at present,
according to Frost & Sullivan.
– 5 –

=== PAGE 16 ===
SUMMARY
High-speed SerDes (Serializer/Deserializer) Serial Interface Technologies
SerDes (Serializer/Deserializer) is a foundational technology in the field of high-speed
interconnects. It is a mainstream time-division multiplexing and point-to-point serial
communication technology. At the transmitter side, SerDes converts multiple low-speed
parallel signals into a high-speed serial signal, which is transmitted through a medium such as
optical fiber or copper cables, and then reconverted it to low-speed parallel signals at the
receiver side. As the physical layer foundation for various high-speed transmission
technologies, including PCIe, USB, and Ethernet, SerDes plays a critical role in enabling
reliable, high-speed data transfer. Its broad applications span servers, heterogeneous
computing, automotive electronics, and communication systems, making it an essential
component in modern high-speed interconnect solutions.
We have consistently invested in the R&D of SerDes technology, achieving significant
breakthroughs that lay a solid foundation for the development of innovative solutions.We have
developed 32GT/s SerDes IP, which has been applied to the PCIe 5.0/CXL 2.0 Retimer, a
product that has secured large-scale procurement from downstream customers in 2024.
Building on this success, we further developed 64GT/s SerDes IP, which has been integrated
into the PCIe 6.x/CXL 3.x Retimer.
We seek to continue advancing the high-speed SerDes technology.We are currently in the
processing of researching and developing PCIe 7.0 SerDes IP, which could support data rates
of up to 128GT/s, positioning us at the forefront of high-speed interconnect solution.
For details, see “Business — Research and Development.”
COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE
The global high-speed interconnect chip market is entering a phase of rapid growth,
driven by the expansion of AI infrastructure and the evolution of server architectures. The
market currently features multiple parallel technological paths. We operate in a competitive
industry, where we face competition from both global and regional players.
Memory interconnect chip market: As the industry transitions from DDR4 to DDR5, the
competitive landscape has remained stable. In 2024, the market remained highly concentrated,
with the Company, Renesas and Rambus being the three dominant players, collectively
accountingforover90%ofthetotalmarketshare.Amongthem,theCompanyrankedfirstwith
a 36.8% market share, according to Frost & Sullivan.These companies have established strong
technical barriers based on years of R&D, deep understanding of industry standards, and
extensive experience in product design and commercialization. In addition, they have built
long-term and robust relationships with customers and ecosystem partners. Strict product
qualification processes also impose high commercial entry barriers for new entrants. As a
result, leading players have formed a dual competitive moat of “technical barrier and customer
lock-in.”

We have established sales and marketing teams dedicated to both domestic and overseas
markets, who proactively identify market opportunities and tailor sales strategies. We sell our
interconnect chips primarily through direct sales, with a small proportion allocated to
distribution channels. We typically opt for distributors to optimize accounts receivable cycles
and to improve the efficiency of customer management.
Our Direct Sales
We directly acquire new direct sale customers primarily through referrals from our
customers and partners along the value chain, targeted marketing to leading industry
participants, and active participation in industry exhibitions. In 2022, 2023 and 2024 and the

amounted to RMB2,692.9 million, RMB2,151.8 million, RMB3,088.2 million and

Non-IFRS Measures
To supplement our consolidated statements of profit or loss which are presented in
accordance with IFRSs, we use adjusted net profit (Non-IFRS measure) and adjusted net profit
margin (Non-IFRS measure), which are not required by, or presented in accordance with,
IFRSs.
– 9 –

=== PAGE 20 ===
SUMMARY
We define adjusted net profit (Non-IFRS measure) as profit for the periods adjusted by
adding back (i) share-based payments, and (ii) listing expenses, which relate to the Global
Offering. Share-based payments which are both equity-settled and cash-settled in nature, and
related to our restrictedAshare incentive schemes for the purpose of providing incentives and
rewards to eligible participants who contribute to the success of the Group’s operations.
Equity-settled share-based payment expenses are non-cash in nature. Cash-settled share-based
payment expenses are required to be remeasured at fair value at each reporting date.
Consequently, they are affected by fluctuations in secondary market share prices, which may
introduce volatility that is not reflective of the Group’s underlying operating performance.
Accordingly, we exclude the impact of these share-based payment expenses, as they are not
indicativeoftheCompany’scoreoperationsoritslong-termdevelopmentprospects.Wedefine
adjusted net profit margin (Non-IFRS measure) as adjusted net profit (Non-IFRS measure) to
divide corresponding revenue of the year/period.
We believe that Non-IFRS measures facilitate the comparisons of operating performance
and provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our
operating performance in the same manner as it helps our management. However, our
presentation of Non-IFRS measures for the periods may not be comparable to similarly titled
measures presented by other companies. The use of Non-IFRS measures has limitations as an
analytical tool, and investors should not consider it in isolation from, or as a substitute for
analysis of, our results of operations or financial condition as reported under IFRSAccounting
Standards. The following tables reconcile Non-IFRS measures with IFRS Accounting
Standards.

RISK FACTORS
Our business and the Global Offering involve certain risks, which are set out in the
section headed “Risk Factors.”You should read that section in its entirety carefully before you
decide to invest in our Shares. Some of the major risks we face include:
 The success of our business is dependent upon our ability to introduce products on
a timely basis with features and performance levels that provide value to our
customers while supporting and anticipating significant industry transitions.
 Products that fail to meet their specifications or are defective could impose
significant costs on us or result in loss of business.
 The semiconductor industry is cyclical, and increased levels of inventory may lead
to oversupply and lower prices, and conversely, if we do not hold sufficient
inventory, we may not be able to satisfy unexpected demand for our products.
 We are investing heavily in our research and development, and such investment may
not generate the results we expect to achieve.
 We are subject to the risk of customer concentration, and our revenue could be
adversely affected if we lose or are prevented from selling to any of our top
customers.
 If we do not keep pace with technological innovations or customers’ increasing
technological requirements, we may not be able to enhance our existing products
and our products may not be competitive, and our operating results may suffer.
 If we are unable to attract, hire, retain and motivate our key engineers and
employees, our business may be harmed.
 We operate in a competitive industry.
 Reliance on third-party suppliers and their technology to manufacturing, assembly,
testing, or packaging of our products presents potential risks, such as supply
shortages, delays or non-compliance, could harm our business.
 We may not be able to adequately protect or enforce our patents, trade secrets and
other intellectual property rights throughout the world, and our efforts to do so may
be costly.

DIVIDEND
During the Track Record Period, we have declared and paid dividend of RMB341.4
million, RMB338.2 million and RMB443.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2022,
2023 and 2024, respectively. On August 29, 2025, we have approved an interim dividend in
2025 for a cash dividend of RMB226.9 million and such dividend was fully paid in October
2025.
Our Company currently does not have a formal standalone dividend policy or pre-
determined dividend payout ratio. As set forth in our Articles of Association, the Company
shall prioritize cash dividends for profit distribution when it is profit-making, has no
undistributed deficit, and possesses ample cash to pay out dividends without disrupting its
regular business operations. Over any three-year period, the cumulative amount of cash
dividends distributed must be at least 30% of the average annual distributable profits for those
three years. The board of Directors shall set a specific annual distribution ratio based on the
Company’s performance in each given year.
Generally, our Board will make dividend proposals, taking into account factors including
ouractualandexpectedresultsofoperations,cashflowandfinancialposition,generalbusiness
conditionsandbusinessstrategies,expectedworkingcapitalrequirementsandfutureexpansion
plans, legal, regulatory and other contractual restrictions, and other factors that our Board
deems to be appropriate. Our Shareholders in a general meeting may approve declaration of
dividends.

RECENT DEVELOPMENTS
Benefiting from AI industry tailwinds and robust market demand, our interconnect chip
shipments have increased significantly, driving substantial year-over-year growth in our full
year financial results in 2025.
Recently, we have learned that the Antitrust Division of the U.S. Department of Justice
commenced a grand jury investigation relating to semiconductors and semiconductor
components and requested us to produce certain materials, including business records and
internal policies, and provide testimony. We are cooperating with such requests. Following the
discussions with our legal advisor on this matter, as of the date of this Prospectus, we
understand that neither we nor any of our Directors has been charged with any wrongdoing.As
of the date of this Prospectus, we are of the view, as advised by our legal advisor on this matter
and taking into account its analysis, considering the current stage of the investigation, we are
not able to predict the timing and outcome, including whether any follow-up actions may be
taken against us and whether charges will or will not be filed against us or others. If there are
any material developments relevant to us on this matter following the Listing, we will disclose
in accordance with the Listing Rules. See also “Risk Factors — Risks Related to Our Business
and Industry — We are subject to scrutiny under antitrust laws and/or could be involved in
related investigations” and “Regulatory Overview — Regulation environment in the U.S. —
U.S. Antitrust Laws .”
InSeptember2025,welaunchedCXL3.1MemoryeXpanderController,nowinsampling
phase with key customers. Our CXL 3.1 Memory eXpander Controller is compliant with the
CXL 3.1 Type 3 specification. Built on a PCIe 6.2 physical layer interface, our CXL 3.1

GLOSSARY
This glossary contains definitions of certain technical terms used in this prospectus
in connection with us and our business. These may not correspond to standard industry
definitions and may not be comparable to similarly terms adopted by other companies.
“AEC” active electrical cables, high-speed data transmission
cables that contain IC to boost signal quality, enabling
longer reach and improved performance compared to
passive cables while using traditional copper conductors
“AI” artificial intelligent
“CAGR” compound annual growth rate
“chip” a miniature electronic device or component that
interconnects essential circuit elements, such as
transistors, diodes, resistors, capacitors and inductors,
through specific wiring methods with semiconductor
fabrication processes into a complete electronic circuit,
which are formed on one or several small semiconductor
wafers or dielectric substrates and encapsulated in a
package
“cluster networking” the network infrastructure and configuration that connect
multiple servers in a computing cluster to enable
high-speed and low latency communication
“CKD” a DDR5 clock driver, a specialized buffer IC used on
client DDR5 memory modules to buffer and re-drive
signals from the memory controller to the DRAM chips,
which improves signal integrity by reducing clock jitter
and loading, supporting higher frequencies for client
modules
“CPU” central processing unit, a mass integrated circuit that
serves as the computational and controlling core of
electronic devices
“CXL” compute express link, an open industry standard high-
speed interconnect that enables efficient, low-latency
communication between CPUs and accelerators, memory
expanders, or other devices, supporting memory
coherence and advanced computing
– 37 –

=== PAGE 48 ===
GLOSSARY
“data center” a complex facility that houses not only computer systems
and related equipment, but also includes redundant data
communication links, environmental controls,
monitoring systems and various security devices, which
provides large-scale, high-quality, secure and reliable
services such as professional server hosting, space
leasing and wholesale bandwidth to internet content
providers and websites
“dB” decibel, a logarithmic unit used to express the ratio
between two values, commonly used to measure signal
strength, power gain/loss, or sound intensity in
electronics and telecommunications
“DB” data buffer, a device used to buffer and re-drive data
signals coming from the memory controller or memory
chips
“DDR” doubledatarate,amemorytechnologyusedtodoublethe
data transfer rate by transmitting data on both the rising
and falling edges of the clock signals
“DFE” decision feedback equalization, a signal processing
technique used in high-speed data communication to
correct inter-symbol interference, which works by using
previously detected bits to subtract expected distortion
from the current signal, improving signal clarity and
reducing error rates
“DIMM” dual in-line memory module, a type of memory module
used in computers, consisting of DRAM chips mounted
on a small circuit board with separate electrical contacts
on each side, allowing for wider data paths and higher
performance compared to older SIMMs
“DRAM” dynamic random access memory, a semiconductor
storage device
“DSC” dynamic security check, a real-time assessment of system
or application behavior to detect security threats
– 38 –

=== PAGE 49 ===
GLOSSARY
“EDSFF” Enterprise & Data Center SSD Form Factor, a solid-state
drive (SSD) form factor standard specifically designed
for enterprise storage systems and data centers, aimed at
delivering storage solutions with higher density,
improved thermal management, and enhanced scalability
“Ethernet” a widely used networking technology that enables
devices to communicate over a local area network using
standardized protocols for data transmission via wired
connections
“fabless” IC design companies that focus solely on IC research,
development and sales, while outsourcing wafer
fabrication, packaging and testing to specialized
foundries and service providers; the term is sometimes
also used to refer to this business model
“foundry” a manufacturer specializing in the production and
manufacture of chips in the field of integrated circuits
“frequency” the rate at which a power electronic device, such as a
switch or rectifier, operates; it is a crucial factor
influencing the performance and efficiency of power
systems
“GPU” A specialized processor primarily designed for rapid
rendering of images and video, which is now widely used
for parallel processing tasks in scientific computing, AI,
and cloud machine learning
“GT/s” gigatransfers per second, a unit measuring data transfer
rate,commonlyusedinPCIExpressandotherhigh-speed
interfaces
“IC” integrated circuit, a small unit or package which is made
as a single indivisible structure (such as a chip) and is
electrically equivalent to a conventional circuit of many
separate components
“IC design” the entire process of circuit function definition, structural
design, circuit design and simulation, layout design and
verification,aswellassubsequentpost-designprocessing
– 39 –

=== PAGE 50 ===
GLOSSARY
“IDM” integrated device manufacturer, whose business scope
covers all stages of the IC value chain, including IC
design, wafer fabrication, packaging and testing and
sales; the term is sometimes also used to refer to this
business model
“I2C” inter-integrated circuit, a multi-master, multi-slave serial
communication protocol that enables low-speed data
exchange between chips on a circuit board using only a
data line and a clock line
“I3C” improved inter-integrated circuit, a high-speed, low-
power communication protocol designed as the successor
to I2C
“I/O” input/output
“JEDEC” Joint Electron Device Engineering Council (now known
as the JEDEC Solid State Technology Association), a
global organization in developing open standards for the
microelectronics industry
“LRDIMM” load reduced dual in-line memory module, a type of
memory module that uses a buffer to reduce the electrical
load on the memory controller, enabling higher memory
capacity and improved signal integrity, particularly in
servers and advanced systems
“MDB” multiplexed rank data buffer, a memory buffer chip that
manages data signals for multiple memory ranks by
multiplexing them, which improves memory system
performance and capacity by efficiently handling data
flow between the memory controller and several DRAM
ranks on a module
“memory” a storage device within an electronic system used to store
programs and data, such as all information in a computer
including input data, computing programs, intermediate
results and final outputs, which stores and retrieves
information according to the addresses specified by the
controller
“MHz” megahertz, a unit of frequency equal to one million
cycles per second
– 40 –

=== PAGE 51 ===
GLOSSARY
“MRCD” multiplexed rank registering clock driver, a specialized
buffer chip used in memory modules to buffer and
re-drive clock, address, and command signals efficiently
across multiple memory ranks, improving signal integrity
and enabling higher memory speeds and capacities
“MRDIMM” multiplexed rank dual in-line memory module, a high-
bandwidth server memory module based on the DDR5
LRDIMM architecture adopting the “1+10” design
consisting of one MRCD chip and 10 MDB chips, which,
compared with RDIMM and LRDIMM, enables
simultaneous access to two memory arrays on the module
and effectively doubles the bandwidth; the first
generation of MRDIMM is also referred to MCRDIMM
by some manufacturers
“MT/s” mega transfers per second, a unit measuring data transfer
rate
“MXC” memory expansion controller, the core chip of high-
bandwidth and high-capacity memory expansion modules
based on the CXL protocol, which connects to the host
via the CXL interface and enables high-bandwidth and
low-latency memory access for server systems
“NIC” network interface card, a hardware component that
connects a computer or server to a network, enabling
communication over local area networks or the internet
“NVMe SSD” non-volatile memory express solid-state drive, a high-
speed storage device that provides fast data transfer, low
latency and efficient access to flash memory
“ODM” original design manufacturer
“OEM” original equipment manufacturer
“packaging” the process of encapsulating the bare die into a finished
chip product with external shell and leads, which is
electrically connected to external pins through wires or
other interconnection methods and then securely closed;
IC packaging not only provides electrical connections
between the internal bonding points of the chip and the
external circuitry, but also offers a stable and reliable
operating environment, ensuring proper functionality,
high stability and long-term reliability
– 41 –

=== PAGE 52 ===
GLOSSARY
“PAM4” four-level pulse amplitude modulation, a high-speed
digital signal modulation technique that encodes data
using four voltage levels, enabling the transmission of
two bits per symbol, which doubles the data rate within
the same bandwidth compared with NRZ technology
“PCIe” peripheral component interconnect express, a high-speed
serial interface standard used to connect components like
graphics cards, SSDs, and NICs to a computer’s
motherboard, offering fast data transfer and scalable
bandwidth through multiple lanes
“PCIe Retimer” a high-speed PCIe signal conditioning chip that
compensates for channel attenuation and mitigates jitter
to enhance signal integrity and extend signal reach,
which serves as a critical interconnect component in
applications such as cloud computing, AI, and data
centers
“PCIe Switch” PCIe switch chip, a core interconnect component in data
centers, AI acceleration systems, and storage systems,
expands PCIe topology to enable efficient
communication among multiple devices, addressing
bandwidth bottleneck issues between hosts and
peripheral devices

GLOSSARY
“PrC” Pre-Check, a hardware-level security checking
mechanism that verifies CPU instructions before
execution to enhance processor safety
“RCD” registering clock driver, a device used to buffer and
re-drive address, command and control signals coming
from the memory controller to DRAM devices
“RDIMM” registereddualin-linememorymodule,atypeofmemory
module that uses RCD chips to buffer address, command,
and control signals. It is mainly used in servers
“R&D” research and development
“Security & Trust Computing a dedicated hardware component designed to offload and
Accelerator” accelerate security functions (e.g., cryptographic
operations, secure boot, authentication, attestation) from
the main CPU, enhancing system security and enabling
trusted computing environments
“SerDes” Serializer/Deserializer, a reusable hardware design block
used in chip design, which enables high-speed serial data
communication by converting parallel data into serial
form for transmission and converting it back on reception
“SoC” system on chip, an application-specific IC that contains a
complete system, including all necessary hardware and
embedded software components, integrated onto a single
chip
“SPD” serial presence detect, a small chip on a memory module
that stores configuration information, such as size, speed,
voltageandtiming,whichthesystemreadsduringbootto
correctly initialize the memory
“SSD” solid-state drive, a storage device that uses flash memory
to store data, offering faster read/write speeds, lower
latency and greater durability compared to traditional
mechanical hard drives
“tape-out” the final stage in the IC design process where the verified
physical design data (photomask sets) is released to the
semiconductor foundry for wafer fabrication

“TCO” total cost of ownership

“1+9”/“1+10” a distributed memory buffer subsystem architecture that
employs one RCD chip working in conjunction with
multiple DB chips, which significantly reduces the load
effect between the CPU and DRAM, lowers signal
transmission loss and addresses the trade-off between
large memory capacity and high speed; this architecture
consistsofoneRCDchipandnineDBchipsintheDDR4

RISK FACTORS
We are exposed to risks associated with U.S. Executive Order14105 and its implementing
regulations that prohibit and require notification by U.S. persons forcertain investments.
On October 28, 2024, the U.S. Department of theTreasury (the “Treasury”) issued a final
rule on outbound investment, or the Outbound Investment Rule, to implement the executive
orderofAugust9,2023,whichbecameeffectiveonJanuary2,2025.TheOutboundInvestment
Rule imposes investment prohibition and notification requirements on U.S. persons for a wide
range of investments in entities associated with China (including Hong Kong and Macau),
collectively defined as “Covered Foreign Persons,” that are engaged in activities relating to
three sectors: (i) semiconductors and microelectronics, (ii) quantum information technologies,
and (iii) artificial intelligence systems. U.S. persons subject to the Outbound Investment Rule
are prohibited from making, or required to report, certain investments in Covered Foreign
Persons, which are defined as “covered transactions.” The Outbound Investment Rule could
apply to certain U.S. person (including their controlled foreign entities, if applicable) outside
the United States who may participate in the Global Offering through offshore transactions in
accordance with Regulation S.
Our Directors are of the view that the Outbound Investment Rule has no material adverse
impact to our business operations, financial performance and the Global Offering. Our
Directors are of the view, as advised by our legal advisor and taking into account its view, that
we are a “covered foreign person” and our business constitutes “covered activities” and
investments by U.S. persons in us may constitute “notifiable transactions” under the Outbound
Investment Rule. However, as of the Latest Practicable Date, the Company does not engage in
any covered activities that would result in a “prohibited transaction” because our business
involving the design of ICs does not meet the performance parameters of the advanced ICs
covered by “prohibited transaction” as defined under the Outbound Investment Rule.
On December 23, 2025, the Treasury published additional frequently asked questions
(“FAQs”) on the Outbound Investment Rule. One of these FAQs (X. 4) provides that absent
additional facts, when a U.S. person acquires an equity interest in a “covered foreign person”,
and at the time of such acquisition the equity interest is publicly traded, such security falls
under the description of a “publicly traded security” in 31 C.F.R. §850.501(a)(1)(i), regardless
of when an agreement to make its investments is entered into. In light of the FAQs’guidance,
we are of the view, as advised by our legal advisor and taking into account its view, a U.S.
person’s acquisition of our H shares that are publicly listed and traded in this Global Offering
may constitute an “excepted transaction” assuming the U.S. person would not also be afforded
rights beyond “standard minority shareholder protections.” While neither the Outbound
Investment Rule nor the FAQs define the time of acquisition, as advised by our legal advisor,
it is reasonable to conclude that the acquisition of the H shares by investors occurs upon
settlement with them since the investors will receive our H shares at settlement.As long as the
settlement of the H shares purchased by U.S. persons occurs after 9:00 am on the Listing Date,
the H shares they acquire would be publicly listed and traded securities. However, if settlement
occurs before 9:00am on the Listing date when the H shares are not yet publicly listed and
traded (for example, this is the case for settlement for Hong Kong Offer Shares), it remains
uncertainwhetherthepubliclytradedsecuritiesexceptionundertheOutboundInvestmentRule
can be applicable.

Investment Rule while making certain modifications. While the COINS Act was legally
enacted and effective on December 18, 2025, it is not self-executing and it does not replace or
amend the Outbound Investment Rule immediately. The COINS Act is a U.S. federal statute
thatprovidesthestatutorybasisoftheOutboundInvestmentRule.TheCOINSActrequiresthe
Treasury to, within 450 days from passage, promulgate new or amended regulations (which
may then amend or replace the Outbound Investment Rule) to implement the law. The
application and implication of the Outbound Investment Rule, the America First Memo, the
COINSAct and any related policies, laws and regulations are complex, which may be changed
and updated from time to time. Future changes in the Outbound Investment Rule, theAmerica
First Memo, the COINS Act and any related policies, laws and regulations or their
interpretations, or any similar or more expansive restrictions imposed by the U.S. or other
jurisdictions, may result in additional costs on our business and/or limit our ability to raise
capital or contingent equity capital from U.S. investors and other sources that may otherwise
be beneficial to us, which could adversely affect our performance, financial condition and
prospects, in which case the offering of our H Shares may also be materially and adversely
affected.

Our Company is a PRC enterprise and is subject to PRC tax on our global income, and

Under the current PRC tax laws and regulations, non-PRC individuals and non-PRC
enterprises are subject to different tax obligations with respect to dividends paid to them by us
and any gains realized upon the sale or other disposition of our H Shares.
Non-PRC individuals are generally subject to PRC individual income tax under the
Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國個人所得稅法》) with respect to
PRC source income or gains at a rate of 20%. We are required to withhold related tax from
dividend payments paid to non-PRC resident individuals, unless specifically exempted by the
tax authority of the State Council or reduced or eliminated by an applicable tax treaty.
However, pursuant to the Circular on Certain Policy Questions Concerning Individual Income
Tax issued by the MOF and SAT (《財政部、國家稅務總局關於個人所得稅若干政策問題的通
知》) on May 13, 1994, dividends and bonuses income gained by foreign individuals from
foreign-invested enterprises is exempted from individual income tax for the time being.
According to the Circular Declaring that Individual Income Tax Continues to
Be Exempted over Individual Income from Transfer of Shares issued by the MOF and
the STA (《財政部、國家稅務總局關於個人轉讓股票所得繼續暫免徵收個人所得稅的通知》)
effective as of March 30, 1998, income from individuals’transfer of stocks of listed companies
continued to be temporarily exempted from individual income tax. On February 3, 2013, the
State Council approved and promulgated the Notice of Suggestions to Deepen the Reform of
System of Income Distribution (《國務院批轉發展改革委等部門關於深化收入分配制度改革
若干意見的通知》). On February 8, 2013, the General Office of the State Council promulgated
the Circular ConcerningAllocation of Key Works to Deepen the Reform of System of Income
Distribution (《國務院辦公廳關於深化收入分配制度改革重點工作分工的通知》). According
to these two documents, the PRC government is planning to cease foreign individuals’ tax
exemption for their dividends and bonuses income obtained from foreign-invested enterprises,
and the MOF and the SAT should be responsible for making and implementing details of such
plan. However, relevant implementation rules or regulations have not been promulgated by the
MOF and the SAT. Considering the situations, non-resident individual holders of our H Shares
should be aware that they may be obligated to pay PRC income tax on dividend and bonuses
income realized from the H Shares.

providesthattherequirementinRule8.12oftheListingRulesmaybewaivedbyhavingregard
to, among other considerations, our arrangements for maintaining regular communication with
the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

requirements of the Listing Rules. Therefore, we have appointed Ms. Lai Siu Kuen (“Ms.
Lai”), a fellow member of The Hong Kong Chartered Governance Institute and The Chartered
Governance Institute in the United Kingdom, who fully meets the requirements stipulated
under Rules 3.28 and 8.17 of the Listing Rules to act as the other joint company secretary. Ms.
Lai provide assistance to Ms. Fu for an initial period of three years from the Listing Date to
enable Ms. Fu to acquire the “relevant experience” under Note 2 to Rule 3.28 of the Listing
Rules so as to fully comply with the requirements set forth under Rules 3.28 and 8.17 of the
Listing Rules.
Since Ms. Fu does not possess the qualifications required of a company secretary under
Rule 3.28 of the Listing Rules, we have applied to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange for, and the
Hong Kong Stock Exchange has granted us, a waiver from strict compliance with the
requirements under Rules 3.28 and 8.17 of the Listing Rules for a three-year period from the
Listing Date, such that Ms. Fu may be appointed as a joint company secretary of our Company
on the conditions that (i) Ms. Lai is appointed as a joint company secretary to assist Ms. Fu
in discharging her functions as a company secretary and in gaining the relevant experience
underRule3.28oftheListingRules;thewaiverwillberevokedimmediatelyifMs.Lai,during
the three-year period, ceases to provide assistance to Ms. Fu as the joint company secretary;
and (ii) the waiver would be revoked if there are material breaches of the Listing Rules by the
Company. In addition, Ms. Fu will comply with the annual professional training requirement
under Rule 3.29 of the Listing Rules and will enhance her knowledge of the Listing Rules
during the three-year period from the Listing. Ms. Fu will also be assisted by (a) our
ComplianceAdviser, particularly in relation to compliance with the Listing Rules; and (b) the
Hong Kong legal advisers of our Company, on matters concerning our Company’s ongoing
compliance with the Listing Rules and the applicable laws and regulations.
Before the expiration of the initial three-year period, the qualifications of Ms. Fu will be
re-evaluated to determine whether the requirements as stipulated in Rules 3.28 and 8.17 of the
Listing Rules can be satisfied. We will liaise with and demonstrate to the Hong Kong Stock
Exchange to enable it to assess whether Ms. Fu, having benefited from the assistance of Ms.
Lai for the preceding three years, will have acquired the skills necessary to carry out the duties
of company secretary and the relevant experience within the meaning of Note 2 to Rule 3.28
of the Listing Rules so that a further waiver will not be necessary.

DISCLOSURE OF OFFER PRICE
Paragraph 15(2)(c) ofAppendix D1Ato the Listing Rules provides that the issue price or
offer price of each security must be disclosed in the prospectus. Pursuant to Paragraph 12 of
the Guide, the Stock Exchange also allows an indicative offer price range to be included in the
prospectus, as an alternative to the disclosure of a fixed offer price.
We have applied to the Stock Exchange a waiver from strict compliance with paragraph
15(2)(c) of Appendix D1A to the Listing Rules so that the Company will only disclose the
maximum Offer Price in the Prospectus on the below basis:
(a) the Offer Price will be determined with reference to, among other factors, the
closingpriceoftheCompany’sASharesontheShanghaiStockExchangeonthelast
trading day on or before the Price Determination Date. Our Company is unable to
control the trading price of our A Shares on the Shanghai Stock Exchange;
(b) setting a fixed offer price or an offer price range with a low-end may adversely
affect our ability to price our H Shares in the best interests of our Shareholders and
the market price of the A Shares and the Hong Kong Offer Shares;
(c) pursuant to paragraphs 9 and 10(b) of the Third Schedule to the Companies
(Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance, the amount payable on
application and allotment on each share, and the price to be paid for shares
subscribed for, shall be specified in the Prospectus, respectively. Disclosure of a
maximum offer price complies with the requirements prescribed under paragraphs 9
and 10(b) of the Third Schedule to the Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous
Provisions) Ordinance by providing a clear indication of the maximum subscription
consideration a potential investor shall pay for the Offer Shares; and
(d) a maximum Offer Price will be disclosed in this prospectus. This alternative
disclosure approach would not prejudice the interests of the investing public in
Hong Kong.
The Stock Exchange has granted to us a waiver from strict compliance with paragraph

disclose:
(a) the maximum Offer Price;

Rule 10.04 of the Listing Rules requires that a person who is an existing shareholder of
a listing applicant may only subscribe for or purchase any securities for which listing is sought
that are being marketed by or on behalf of a listing applicant either in his/her/its own name or
through nominees if the conditions in Rule 10.03 of the Listing Rules are fulfilled, namely that
(i) no securities are to be offered to the existing shareholders on a preferential basis and no
preferential treatment is given to them in the allocation of the securities; and (ii) the minimum
prescribed percentage of public shareholders required by Rule 8.08(1) of the Listing Rules is
achieved. Paragraph 1C(2) of Appendix F1 to the Listing Rules states that, without the prior
written consent of the Stock Exchange, no allocations will be permitted to be made to directors
orexistingshareholdersofalistingapplicantortheircloseassociates,unlesstheconditionsset
out in Rules 10.03 and 10.04 are fulfilled.
Chapter 4.15 of the Guide provides that the Stock Exchange will consider granting a
waiver from Rule 10.04 of the Listing Rules and a consent, pursuant to paragraph 1C(2) of
Appendix F1 to the Listing Rules, to allow a listing applicant’s existing shareholders or their
closeassociatestoparticipateinitsinitialpublicofferingifanyactualorperceivedpreferential
treatment arising from their ability to influence the listing applicant during the allocation
process can be addressed.
Prior to the Listing, our share capital comprises entirely A Shares listed on the Shanghai
Stock Exchange STAR Market. As a company listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR
Market with itsAShares publicly traded thereon and with a large publicAShares shareholder
base, it would be unduly burdensome for us to seek the prior consent of the Stock Exchange
for each of our minority existing Shareholders or their close associates who subscribe for the
H Shares in the Global Offering.

GLOBAL HIGH-SPEED INTERCONNECT CHIP MARKET OVERVIEW
Definition and Classification of High-Speed Interconnect Chips
High-speedinterconnectchipsarevitalcomponentsenablinghigh-speeddataconnectand
exchange in data centers, servers, and computers. They address bottlenecks in data
transmissionarisingfromcontinuousupgradestointelligentcomputingsystems.Bysupporting
multiple standardized communication protocols and leveraging technologies such as signal
processing and architecture optimization, these chips ensure efficient and reliable data transfer
across various systems.
High-speedinterconnectchipsarecategorizedintothreeprimarytechnicaltypes:memory
interconnect chips, PCIe/CXL interconnect chips, and Ethernet & optical interconnect chips.
Memoryinterconnectchips,includingmemoryinterfaceandmodulesupportingchips,enhance
the speed and stability of memory data access. PCIe/CXL interconnect chips, such as PCIe
Retimers, PCIe Switches, CXL MXC, and CXL Switches, facilitate multi-card connections
within servers, memory pooling, and memory expansion in data centers and servers. Ethernet
& optical interconnect chips, including Ethernet Retimers/Switches, oDSPs, NICs, and silicon
photonics chips, are tailored for long-distance, high-bandwidth interconnection solutions such
as cluster networking in data centers.
Key Drivers of the High-Speed Interconnect Chip Market
 Explosive Data Growth Drives Soaring Demand for Data Interaction: Global data is
growing exponentially, with the generated data volume expected to reach 197.3
Zettabytes (ZB, a unit of one sextillion bytes) in 2025 and surge to 635.3 ZB by 2030,
representing a CAGR of 26.3%.The proliferation of massive data has triggered explosive
growth in demand for data processing and interaction. As the vital cornerstone for data
transmission, high-speed interconnect chips have seen a corresponding surge in potential
demand.
– 122 –

=== PAGE 133 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
 Upgraded Transmission Performance Highlights Chip Value: Standardized
communication protocols are evolving continuously, driving persistent improvements in
transmission rates. Take the PCIe protocol as an example — each iteration doubles the
transmission speed, but this acceleration also exacerbates issues such as signal
attenuation and signal integrity. High-speed interconnect chips effectively address these
challenges, making their necessity and value in data transmission increasingly prominent.
 Complex Computing Architectures Drive Chip Demand Expansion: The launch of
ChatGPT in 2022 ignited demand forAI training, while the accelerated deployment ofAI
applications since 2024 has spurred demand for AI inference. The training and inference
of large models are profoundly transforming the architecture ofAI servers, shifting from
merely increasing the number of servers to adopting a “Strong Scaling” model. This
approach constructs high-bandwidth, low-latency computing clusters by enhancing
memory bandwidth and increasing network hardware density.This transformation has led
to a surge in interconnection demands, including among chips, server chassis, server
clusters, and data centers, thereby imposing higher requirements on the quantity and
complexity of high-speed interconnect chips.
Global Demand in the Server and PC Markets
High-speed interconnect chips are primarily used in servers with some applications in
personal computers.
The increasing demand for high-speed interconnects inAI servers has become one of the
factors supporting the expansion of the high-speed interconnect chip market. Global shipments
ofAI servers increased from 0.5 million units in 2020 to 2.0 million units in 2024, representing
a CAGR of 45.2%. Looking ahead, shipments are projected to grow from 2.5 million units in
2025 to 6.5 million units in 2030, with a CAGR of 21.2%. The growth inAI server demand is
associated with computing workloads that require higher bandwidth and more efficient data
exchange.Multichipclusterarchitecturesrequirehigh-bandwidth,low-latencyinterconnectsto
support large-scale data interactions, contributing to the demand for PCIe/CXL interconnect
chipsaswellasEthernetandopticalinterconnectchips.Additionally,thistrenddrivestheneed
for system main memory with larger capacities and higher bandwidths. As AI servers adopt
architectures featuring multi-card interconnection and high-speed protocols, the demand for
high-speed interconnect chips supporting next-generation standards such as PCIe 6.0 and CXL
3.0 will continue to rise. The demand in the general server market is relatively stable, but also
requires high-speed interconnect chips to enhance data-access stability. Although its growth
rate is more moderate compared with AI servers, the general server market remains an
important pillar for the chip market.

Future Potential of the High-Speed Interconnect Chip Market Driven by AI
In the AI era, particularly with the explosive development of large models, the demand
for high-speed interconnects in data centers and servers has grown exponentially, directly
driving the expansion of the high-speed interconnect chip market. Moore’s Law continues to
propel semiconductor advancements, necessitating innovative interconnect products to
overcome bandwidth bottlenecks in increasingly heterogeneous computing architectures.
Meanwhile, the Scaling Law demonstrates that AI model performance improves with the
expansion of model size, training dataset scale, and computational load (FLOPs), which
imposes increasingly stringent requirements on data transmission bandwidth and memory
access efficiency. The Scaling Law makes high-speed interconnect chips a critical enabling
technology for AI computing power expansion. The global market size of high-speed
interconnect chips reached USD15.4 billion in 2024 and is projected to further grow to
USD49.0 billion by 2030, with a CAGR of 21.2%. Among them, the Chinese market has
become one of the fastest-growing segments. In 2024, its market size accounted for
approximately 25% of the global total, and it is expected to rise to 30% by 2030. The main
reason for this increase in market share is that the demand forAI servers in China is projected
to grow faster than the global average in the future.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
GLOBAL MEMORY INTERCONNECT CHIP MARKET
Definition and Classification of Memory Interconnect Chips
Memory interconnect chips serve as core components for enabling high-speed memory
data transmission and stable access. The traditional product portfolio includes memory
interface chips (RCD/DB) and memory module supporting chips (SPD, TS, PMIC). With the
development ofAI and big data applications and related technological advancements, memory
interconnect chips have derived categories adapted to new computing power requirements,
including MRCD/MDB chips for server memory and CKD chips for PC memory. From a
pricing perspective, different product types exhibit substantial variation, with unit prices
ranging from approximately USD0.2 to USD16.0.
 Memory Interface Chips (RCD/DB)
Memory interface chips (Registering Clock Driver/Data Buffer) are the core logic
components of server memory modules. They serve as the necessary data pathway
between the CPU and memory, with the primary function of enhancing memory data
access speed and reliability.
According to functional classification under DDR4 and DDR5 standards, memory
interfacechipsaredividedintotwotypes:RCD(RegisteringClockDrivers),whichbuffer
address, command, clock, and control signals from the memory controller; and DB
(Data Buffers), which buffer data signals from either the memory controller or DRAM
chips.MemorymodulesthatonlyuseRCDsareknownasRDIMMs(RegisteredDIMMs),
while modules using both RCD and DB are known as LRDIMMs (Load Reduced
DIMMs). Under JEDEC standards, each DDR4 or DDR5 server memory module
(RDIMM/LRDIMM)includesoneRCDchip.DBchipisusedinLRDIMMwhichDDR4
requires nine DB chips and DDR5 requires ten DB chips.
 Supporting Chips for Memory Modules (SPD, TS, PMIC)
According to JEDEC standards, DDR5 memory modules must include, in addition
toDRAMchipsandinterfacechips,threetypesofsupportingchips:SPD(SerialPresence
Detect), TS (Temperature Sensor), and PMIC (Power Management Integrated Circuit).
The SPD (Serial Presence Detect) incorporates an onboard EEPROM (Electrically
Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory), which is used to store information related
to the memory module, including configuration parameters of memory chips and
associated components on the module. Additionally, the SPD serves as an I2C/I3C bus
hub, acting as the communication center between the system’s main controller and the
components on the memory module. The SPD also integrates a TS to monitor the
temperature at its location.TheTS is a high-precision temperature sensor chip for DDR5,
compliant with JEDEC standards, and supports I2C and I3C serial buses, enabling
temperature monitoring of the memory module. The PMIC supplies power to other chips
on the memory module and handles power management.
– 126 –

=== PAGE 137 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Under JEDEC standards, each DDR4 and DDR5 server memory module includes
one SPD. In addition, each DDR5 RDIMM / LRDIMM / MRDIMM also requires one
PMIC and two TSs. Mainstream DDR4 and DDR5 PC memory modules typically include
one SPD, whereas DDR5 PC memory modules also require one PMIC. SPD in DDR5
memory module is more complex and has higher value than that in DDR4.
 MRCD/MDB Chips
MRCD and MDB chips are the core logic components of high-bandwidth memory
modules known as MRDIMMs (Multiplexer Ranks DIMMs). Each MRDIMM requires
one MRCD and ten MDB chips. MDB chips allow simultaneous access to two DRAM
ranks (whereas traditional RDIMMs can only access one), effectively doubling the
bandwidth at standard data rates. These chips are primarily used in cloud computing and
AI applications with stringent memory bandwidth requirements.
 Clock Driver Chips (CKD)
As defined by JEDEC, when DDR5 data rates reach 6,400MT/s and above, PC
memory modules are required to integrate CKD (Clock Driver) chips to buffer and
re-drive the clock signal. This ensures the integrity and reliability of high-speed clock
signals, which are critical for stable operation at such data rates. CKD is used in high-rate
transmission PCs, generally a PC memory module needs to be equipped with one CKD.
Typically, one PC is equipped with 1 to 2 memory module.

Growth and Future Potential of the Memory Interconnect Chip Market
Memory interconnect chips are primarily used in servers, with some also applied in PCs.
The market size is closely linked to the shipment volume of servers and PCs, as well as the
types and quantities of memory modules configured per unit.
Global Market Demand for Memory Modules
From 2020 to 2024, global memory module shipments increased from 158.2 million units
to 170.4 million units, and are expected to reach 306.6 million units by 2030, representing a
CAGR of approximately 10.8% from 2025 to 2030, indicating a strong growth trajectory.
Structurally, the server memory module market is rapidly transitioning to the DDR5
generation: DDR5 began entering downstream markets in 2021, surpassed 50% penetration by
2024, and is projected to exceed 85% in 2025. Meanwhile, DDR6 memory modules are
anticipated to reach commercial adoption around 2029, bringing new growth momentum to the
market.
The primary drivers behind the rising demand for server memory modules include the
continued growth in global server shipments and the increasing number of memory modules
configured per server. The rise of AI servers further accelerates demand. Due to significantly
higher memory capacity requirements, typically one general server is equipped with 8 to 12
memory modules while one AI server is equipped with 16 to 24 memory modules. As AI
technology is increasingly adopted across industries, the penetration rate of AI servers
continues to rise, directly driving memory module demand to grow faster than overall server
shipments. This trend is expected to create substantial growth opportunities for the memory
interconnect chip market.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Key Growth Drivers in the Server Segment
Growth in Memory Module Demand Drives Expansion of the Market
Memory interconnect chips have a well-defined deployment ratio with memory modules,
makingtheirdemandcloselycorrelated.AccordingtoFrost&Sullivan,servermemorymodule
demand will grow from 183.9 million units in 2025 to 306.6 million units in 2030. This
significant growth directly drives a proportional increase in memory interconnect chip
shipments, laying a solid foundation for market expansion.
Product Upgrades Create a New Growth Opportunity
 DDR5 technological advancements increase chip value: With higher technical
complexity and enhanced performance, DDR5 RCD and SPD chips offer significantly
higher unit value than their DDR4 counterparts. Additionally, DDR5 server memory
modules require new supporting chips such as TS and PMIC. These upgrades not only
boost per-unit pricing but also expand the chip variety, driving growth in the DDR5 era.
 Emergence of MRDIMM unlocks incremental market potential: Driven by the rising
need for memory bandwidth in AI applications, MRDIMM, known for its superior
bandwidth performance, is expected to become the preferred main memory in mainstream
AI servers. Commercial adoption will begin in 2025, with a projected penetration rate of
30% in AI servers by 2030 and shipments reaching 53.4 million units, with a CAGR of
148.0%from2025to2030.ComparedtothewidelyappliedRDIMM,whichrequiresonly
one RCD, MRDIMM requires a higher-value MRCD and ten additional MDB chips,
significantly boosting the total market value as its penetration rises.
 Successive generational iterations sustain ASP: DDR5 RCD chips are expected to roll
out in six product generations, while MRCD/MDB chips will have three. These
continuous generational upgrades will leverage innovation and performance optimization
to sustain average selling prices and profit margins, ensuring long-term stable growth for
the memory interconnect chip market.
Key Growth Drivers in the PC Segment
 Transition from DDR4 to DDR5 Adds New Chip Requirements: In the PC segment,
DDR5 memory modules (including UDIMM, SODIMM, CAMM, and LPCAMM) require
a higher-spec, higher-value SPD chip and an additional PMIC, collectively driving up
per-unit chip value in the DDR5 era.
 Enhanced Data Rate Support of DDR5 Further Drives the Expansion of Chip
Demand: The first generation of DDR5 supports speeds of 4,800 MT/s. As data rates
reach 6,400 MT/s and beyond, PC memory modules (including CUDIMM, CSODIMM,
and CAMM) will require the addition of a CKD chip. This chip is expected to begin
penetratingthemarketfrom2025andachievenear-totalcoverageinPCmemorymodules
by 2029, opening a new growth avenue in the consumer segment.

Development Trends in the Memory Interconnect Chip Market
 Explosive Computing Power Drives Demand for Memory Capacity and Bandwidth:
The urgent need for computing power in large model training and inference continues to
push for upgrades in memory capacity and bandwidth. Large models represented by GPT,
with parameter scales exceeding trillions, have driven significant upgrades in AI server
memory deployment — each mainstream AI server typically deploys over 20 DDR5
memory modules, with capacity and quantity far exceeding general servers. Meanwhile,
the explosion in computing power has also imposed higher requirements on memory
bandwidth: DDR5 first-generation RDIMM supports a speed of 4,800MT/s, the sixth
generation is expected to exceed 9,000MT/s, and the second-generation MRDIMM
reaches 12,800MT/s. As technology matures and the ecosystem improves, MRDIMM is
expected to replace RDIMM as the mainstream solution for AI servers due to its higher
bandwidth and comprehensive performance, driving a surge in demand for MRCD/MDB
chips. In the PC sector, DDR5 is accelerating its penetration in high-end terminals such
as gaming laptops andAI PCs, with module speeds gradually iterating to 6400 MT/s and
above.To ensure signal integrity at high speeds, it is expected that by 2029, almost all PC
memory modules will be standard-equipped with CKD chips.
 Significantly Shortened Technical Iteration Cycle: The technology of memory
interconnect chips is rapidly evolving along the path of “protocol upgrades —
transmission rate enhancements — increasing chip functional complexity.” Core
competitive advantages are shifting toward high-speed signal processing and low-power
design, driving continuous growth in the value of memory interconnect chips. In the
server domain, DDR4 experienced only four sub-generations, each with an iteration cycle
of approximately 18 to 24 months. In contrast, DDR5 is expected to have six
sub-generations. As of 2024, shipments of the second-generation DDR5 products have
already surpassed those of the first generation, and the third-generation is projected to
ramp up rapidly in 2025. Currently, the iteration cycle per sub-generation has gradually
shortened to 12-18 months, marking a significantly faster pace of technological
advancement compared to the DDR4 era.
 Continuous Enhancement of Market Concentration: From the historical development
of the memory interconnect chip market, leading industry players have established
comprehensive memory interconnect solutions by leveraging extensive product
portfolios, deep technical expertise, and well-developed patent strategies. These
companies play a leading role in standards development and technological innovation,
holding significant competitive advantages. As a result, market share is gradually
concentrating among a few top-tier companies. Looking ahead, these leading enterprises
are expected to further strengthen their market competitiveness and expand their market
share by capitalizing on their existing advantages — such as investing proactively in
next-generation technology R&D and optimizing supply chain management. This will
drive more efficient integration and rational allocation of resources across the industry.

Entry Barriers and Key Success Factors in the Memory Interconnect Chip Market
 Technological Accumulation Creates High Industry Barriers: Memory interconnect
chips fall under the category of high-speed, nonlinear analog and mixed-signal circuits,
making their R&D extremely complex. Success in this field requires not only profound
technical expertise but also long-term accumulation of intellectual property and design
experience. Products in this domain adhere to JEDEC industry standards. To establish a
competitive edge, companies must actively participate in or even lead the development of
these standards, which involves close collaboration and technical exchanges with major
CPU, memory, server, and cloud computing vendors, all while advancing product R&D
in tandem. This closed-loop system of “standards — technology — industry chain”
creates significant barriers for new entrants, as they must not only overcome technical
challenges but also deeply understand industry standards and rapidly introduce
competitive next-generation products in line with standard updates.
 Ecosystem Collaboration Builds Competitive Moats: Memory interconnect chips are
primarily used in servers, where product reliability requirements are stringent, leading to
high commercial entry barriers.Acompany’s core competitiveness largely stems from the
collaborative barriers formed through partnerships with leading ecosystem players. To
maintain their advantage, industry leaders must meet two key criteria: (i) continuously
securing certifications from industry giants across multiple industry chain links
(including memory and CPU manufacturers) for new product generations; and (ii)
maintaining a long track record of stable, high-quality product deliveries. Once
established, these deep partnerships enable leading companies to form a stable ecosystem
closed-loop with industry chain partners in standard-setting and collaborative
development, reinforcing their market position.
GLOBAL PCIe/CXL INTERCONNECT CHIP MARKET
PCIe Interconnect Chip Market Overview and Market Size
Definition and Classification of PCIe Interconnect Chips
PCIe interconnect chips serve as core components for high-speed data interconnection in
data centers and servers, adhering to the PCI-SIG standard system. Their main products are
categorized into two major types:
 PCIe Retimer chips are ultra-high-speed signal conditioning devices designed for
the PCIe protocol. They primarily address issues such as timing skew, severe signal
loss, and poor signal integrity in high-speed, long-distance data transmission
scenarios. These chips play a critical role in interconnections between the CPU and
high-speed peripherals such as GPUs, AI accelerators, SSDs, and NICs. From a
pricing perspective, different product types show significant variation. The average
industry ASP in 2024 was ranged from approximately USD25.0 to USD50.0 per
chip.
– 132 –

=== PAGE 143 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
 PCIe Switch chips are used to expand PCIe lane availability, enabling high-speed
data switching between CPUs and peripheral devices (e.g., NICs, SSDs, GPUs)
through an internal switching architecture, thereby supporting high-density PCIe
interconnections for a larger number of devices. From a pricing perspective,
different product types exhibit substantial variation, with chip prices largely
determined by the number of supported lanes. The industry’s average ASP in 2024
ranged from approximately USD600.0 to USD1,200.0 per chip.
In recent years, the iteration of PCIe protocol technology has accelerated: upgraded from
PCIe 5.0 (32GT/s) to PCIe 6.0 (64GT/s), the transmission rate has doubled, and the newly
released PCIe 7.0 specification further increases the single-channel rate to 128GT/s. In terms
of downstream applications, chips and devices supporting the PCIe 5.0 protocol are becoming
the market mainstream. In the future, the technology will continue to evolve towards higher
speed, lower latency and low power consumption to meet the high-speed interconnection
requirements of emerging scenarios such as AI servers.
Market Size of PCIe Interconnect Chips
The global PCIe interconnect chip market experienced rapid expansion, growing from
USD469.2 million in 2022 to USD2,288.6 million in 2024, and it is expected to enter a phase
of explosive growth, with the market size projected to reach USD7,761.0 million in 2030, with
a CAGR of 20.1% from 2025 to 2030.

Key Growth Drivers for the PCIe Interconnect Chip Market
 Surging AI server shipments drive volume expansion in chip demand: In AI server
architectures, the increasing number of GPUs/AI chips and the rapid expansion of AI
model sizes are significantly driving system bandwidth and high-speed interconnect
requirements. PCIe interconnect chips have become essential components for high-speed
interconnection between devices. PCIe Switches provide expansion and aggregation
capabilities, allowing more devices to connect to a single PCIe port. PCIe Retimers help
maintain signal integrity and system stability by extending the effective transmission
distance for high-speed signals. For example, a mainstream 8-GPU AI server typically
requires 2 to 4 PCIe Switches for topology expansion and 8 to 16 Retimers to extend
connections between CPUs and peripherals. As such, PCIe interconnect chips have
become indispensable toAI server infrastructure, with their demand directly correlated to
AI server shipment volumes.
 Continuous PCIe protocol evolution expands application boundaries: PCIe 5.0 is
becoming the mainstream standard and will continue evolving toward PCIe 6.0 and PCIe
7.0, with each iteration doubling the data transfer rate. This evolution drives two major
growth dynamics: First, higher data rates introduce more complex signal integrity
challenges, expanding the application of PCIe Retimers from CPU and GPU/AI
accelerator/SSD/NIC connections to include active electrical cables (AEC), edge
computing devices, smart vehicles, and other connection-intensive scenarios. Second,
protocol upgrades promote more sophisticated server cluster topologies. PCIe Switches
are increasingly needed for bandwidth optimization and topology expansion across
multiple devices, especially in AI inference workloads and high-density data center
deployments, further elevating their strategic importance.
CXL Interconnect Chip Market Overview and Market Size
Definition and Classification of the CXL Interconnect Chip Market
CXL interconnect chips are core high-speed interconnection devices built based on the
CXL protocol. Their physical layer follows the PCIe standard, enabling high-speed and
low-latency data interaction among CPUs, GPUs, and memory. They are primarily applied in
memory expansion and memory pooling scenarios, with main products categorized into two
types. From a pricing perspective, as CXL adoption and ecosystem development are still at an
early stage and products have not yet reached large-scale commercial shipment, pricing has not
formed a mature structure. Existing products generally range from approximately US$100 to
over US$1,000 per chip, depending on specifications and functionality.
 CXL MXC Chips: Serving as the high-speed connection hub between processors
and CXL memory modules, they undertake protocol conversion, memory access
scheduling, and cache coherence managements. As key controllers for building
memory expansion and memory pooling architectures, they ensure seamless data
management across hardware nodes.

 CXL Switch Chips: It enables interconnection and resource management among
multiple CXLhosts and devices, supporting the connection of one or multiple CPUs
to multiple CXL memory or accelerator devices. This enhances system scalability
and resource utilization efficiency, serving as a core enabling component for
large-scale memory pooling architectures.
These two categories work in tandem to form CXL interconnection solutions, which will
play a pivotal role in next-generation data center architectures.

Entry Barriers and Key Success Factors of PCIe/CXL Interconnect Chips
 Protocol-Driven Technical Iteration and Innovation Capability: The core
competitiveness of PCIe/CXL interconnect chips is rooted in rapid response to protocol
standard evolution and underlying technical breakthroughs. Enterprises need to keep pace
with the accelerating protocol iterations — from PCIe 5.0 to 6.0 and even 7.0, and from
CXL 1.0 to 3.x — by continuously investing in R&D to overcome key technological
challenges such as signal processing and coding algorithms. As the PCIe protocol
upgrades, optimization of high-speed SerDes serial interface technology is essential to
solve issues such as signal attenuation and timing jitter in high-frequency transmission,
ensuring chip compatibility and stability. Meanwhile, CXLtechnology is evolving toward
bandwidth doubling, latency optimization, and function expansion — supporting memory
pooling and point-to-point direct connection, while potentially combining with optical
interconnection to break throughTB-level bandwidth and sub-50ns latency bottlenecks in
the future. At the underlying level, SerDes, as the “nerve center” of high-speed serial
transmission, determines the stability and latency performance of interconnect chips
through speed enhancement (e.g., 64GT/s required for PCIe 6.0) and signal integrity
optimization. DDR controller technology, meanwhile, influences memory access
efficiency and serves as a key technical node for supporting CXL memory pooling.

 Deep Demand Insight and Ecosystem Collaboration Capability: Another core success

GLOBAL ETHERNET AND OPTICAL INTERCONNECT CHIP MARKET
Ethernet Interconnect Chips
Ethernet interconnect chips are core hardware components in data centers, cloud
computing, and AI infrastructure. They enable high-speed data exchange and low-latency
communication between devices. These chips are mainly classified into three categories: (i)
Ethernet Switches, which handle packet forwarding and traffic management and serve as the
backboneofdatacenternetworks;(ii)NICs,whicharedeployedonserversasthekeyinterface
for connecting the host to the Ethernet and enabling data transmission; and (iii) Ethernet
Retimers, which address timing distortion and signal attenuation in long-distance high-speed
signal transmission, ensuring data integrity and system stability, particularly critical for AI
servers and cloud computing nodes.
The global Ethernet interconnect chip market grew from USD6.0 billion in 2020 to
USD9.4 billion in 2024, with a CAGR of 11.6%, primarily driven by the expansion of cloud
computing and digital infrastructure. In future, the accelerated deployment of largeAI models,
AI servers, hyperscale data centers, and high-bandwidth storage systems is generating surging
demandforhigh-speed,low-latencynetworking.As400Gand800GEthernetsolutionsbecome
mainstream and the market moves toward 1.6T, both the demand and value of Ethernet
interconnect chips are expected to increase significantly. The global market is projected to
reach USD24.7 billion by 2030, with a CAGR of 17.9% from 2025 to 2030.
– 137 –

=== PAGE 148 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Optical Interconnect Chips
Optical interconnect chips are essential components that enable high-speed data
transmission through optoelectronic conversion, serving as a core technology for next-
generation high-bandwidth, power-efficient interconnects in data centers andAI infrastructure.
These chips are generally classified into three categories:
 oDSPs, responsible for high-speed signal modulation/demodulation, waveform
shaping, and DSP error correction, indispensable for advanced modulation formats
such as 400G and 800G;
 Drivers and TIAs, where Drivers convert electrical signals into high-frequency
analog signals to drive optical transmitters, and TIAs amplify weak current signals
from photodiodes into voltage signals, enabling high-speed, high-sensitivity
reception;
 Silicon photonic chips, which enable compact, high-speed optical interconnects by
integrating photonic and electronic components on silicon, addressing bandwidth
and power challenges in advanced computing systems.
The global optical interconnect chip market surged from USD0.4 billion in 2020 to
USD2.6 billion in 2024, representing a CAGR of 57%. This growth was primarily driven by
the large-scale deployment of 400G/800G optical modules inAI data centers. In future, as the
number of AI chips in large AI training clusters continues to grow and the demand for
bandwidth density and energy efficiency between nodes accelerates, optical interconnects will
becomeacriticalpartofadvancedsystemarchitectures.Theglobalmarketisexpectedtoreach
USD9.9 billion by 2030, with a CAGR of 21.5% from 2025 to 2030.

Overview of Market Competitive Landscape
The global high-speed interconnect chip market is entering a phase of rapid growth,
driven by the expansion of AI infrastructure and the evolution of server architectures. The
market currently features multiple parallel technological paths.
Memory interconnect chip market: As the industry transitions from DDR4 to DDR5, the
competitive landscape has remained stable with the Company, Renesas and Rambus being the
three dominant players, who together account for over 90% of the market share. These
companies have established strong technical barriers based on years of R&D, deep
understanding of industry standards, and extensive experience in product design and
commercialization. In addition, they have built long-term and robust relationships with
customers and ecosystem partners. Strict product qualification processes also impose high
commercial entry barriers for new entrants. As a result, leading players have formed a dual
competitive moat of “technical barrier and customer lock-in.”

OVERVIEW OF OTHER MARKETS
Global Clock Chip Market Overview and Future Outlook
As a fundamental component in system-level chips, clock chips play a crucial role in
generating, distributing, and managing clock signals within electronic systems to ensure
synchronized data transmission and processing across modules. Based on functionality, clock
chips are mainly categorized into clock generators, clock buffers and jitter attenuators. They
are widely used in applications such as communication infrastructure, data centers, industrial
automation, automotive electronics, and consumer electronics.
The global clock chip market has entered a stage of steady growth. The market size
expanded from USD1.7 billion in 2020 to USD2.2 billion in 2024, with a CAGR of 5.7%
during the period. In future, as demand continues to rise for high-precision timing solutions in
AI servers, high-speed communications, autonomous driving, and industrial edge computing,
the value contribution of clock chips within system architectures is expected to increase
steadily. In 2030, the global clock chip market is projected to grow to USD3.0 billion, with a
CAGR of 5.3% from 2025 to 2030.
China’ s Server CPU Market Overview and Future Outlook
In recent years, driven by China’s digital economy transformation and the rapid growth
incomputingpowerdemand,China’sserverCPUmarkethasshownasteadyupwardtrend.The
market size increased from USD7.7 billion in 2020 to USD10.8 billion in 2024, with a CAGR
of 8.7% during this period. In future, the market is expected to maintain strong growth
momentum. On one hand, the surging shipments of AI servers will drive sustained expansion
in overall server demand, significantly boosting the need for server CPUs. On the other hand,
the number of GPUs installed per server is also gradually increasing in line with rising server
performance.As a result, China’s server CPU market is expected to reach USD15.4 billion by
2030, with a projected CAGR of 6.6% from 2025 to 2030.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
REGULATORY ENVIRONMENT IN THE PRC
Policies on the IC Industry
In June 2014, the State Council promulgated the National Guideline for Promoting the
Development of the Integrated Circuit Industry. It stated that the development goal of the
integrated circuit industry is to reach internationally advanced levels in the main links of the
integrated circuit industrial chain by 2030, with a number of enterprises entering the
international first tier and achieving leapfrog development. The main tasks and development
priorities are to focus on developing the integrated circuit design industry. By centering on the
industrial chains in key areas, it aims to strengthen collaborative innovation in integrated
circuit design, software development, system integration, content and services, driving the
development of the manufacturing industry through the rapid growth of the design industry.
In July 2020, the State Council announced the Several Policies for Promoting High-
quality Development of the Integrated Circuit Industry and the Software Industry in the New
Era. IC design, equipment, material, packaging and testing enterprises and software enterprises
encouraged by the State shall be exempted from enterprise income tax from the first to the
second year from the profit-making year, and shall be subject to enterprise income tax at a
reduced rate of half of the statutory tax rate of 25% from the third to the fifth year. The State
strongly supports qualified IC enterprises and software enterprises to go public and raise
capital both domestically and abroad. Focus on key core technology R&D of high-end chips,
IC equipment and process technology, IC key materials, IC design tools, basic software,
industrial software, and application software. The State encourage enterprises to register for
exclusive rights to IC layout designs and software copyrights. Support IC enterprises and
software enterprises to apply for intellectual property rights in accordance with the law, and
provide relevant support to those that meet the relevant regulations. Strengthening the
protection of exclusive rights to layout designs of IC and software copyrights in the network
environment, actively developing and applying network copyright protection technologies for
genuine software, and effectively protecting intellectual property rights of IC and software.
Regulations Related to Foreign Investment in the PRC
According to the Company Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from July
1, 2024, the “Company Law”), promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National
People’s Congress (the “NPC Standing Committee”) on December 29, 1993, and revised on
December 29, 2023, limited liability companies and joint-stock limited companies established
within the territory of China are subject to the Company Law. Unless otherwise specified by
the law on foreign investment, foreign-invested enterprises are also governed by the Company
Law.
